Bourignon's La derniere misericorde de Dieu (1681, French), full text translated (188/188 pp). Specific Lerouge/Kloss French MS ritual of the 27th degree (Souverains Commandeurs du Temple, ~1820). 1576 Latin anti-ubiquitarian tract refuting Brandenburg Eucharist articles (vs A. Musculus). Daneau's English-translated works are all distinct (witches, physica, Antichrist, ethics). No English translation of this Eucharistic tract located in any source. We hold the Latin original, ~50/58 pp translated.

Brian Duvick's complete English translation, Proclus: On Plato Cratylus (Duckworth 2007; Bloomsbury 2014, Ancient Commentators series, full text on archive.org), translates this same work. Prior complete English exists; not first. Source-language rule: same work counts even from Greek.

James Sanford's complete English translation 'Of the Vanitie and Uncertaintie of Artes and Sciences' (London, 1569; reprinted 1575, and 1676/1694) is the same work, the source-language Latin original we hold. A 16th-c. complete prior English translation exists, so this is not a first translation.

Tasso's Aminta (our Aldine/Manuzio Italian original) has famous early English translations: Abraham Fraunce, Countess of Pembroke's Ivychurch (1591); Henry Reynolds, Aminta Englisht (1628); John Dancer (1660). Prior complete English long predates us.

Work is Pseudo-Aristotle De Mundo (On the Cosmos/Universe), a canonical classical text. Multiple prior English translations exist: Forster 1914 (Clarendon), Furley/Loeb 1955, Barnes 1984, Thom 2014. Our 1526 Budé Latin edition is the same work; prior English from Greek still counts.

Unique Ogyen Choling manuscript (EAP105-2-1-60): a gtor zlog ritual from the Zabchö Rigdzin Thukthik Vajrakilaya 'gug zer reg phung' cycle. Published English Vajrakilaya translations cover the distinct Putri Reg Phung (spu gri) and Palchen Düpa cycles, not this text. No prior English of this work found; 6/6 pages translated.

Liber pharetrae: 13th-c. Latin Franciscan florilegium (~3,589 quotations, formerly attrib. Bonaventure), 1472 incunabulum. Active scholarly project edits only the Latin (Peltier 1866); no English translation found in any catalog or search. Our copy ~complete (725/735 pp).

Our book is Baeumker's 1895 critical Latin edition of Ibn Gabirol's Fons Vitae, which we translated. A prior complete English translation exists: A. B. Jacob, 'The Fountain of Life,' Philadelphia 1954, rendered from the Latin (same work). Wedeck 1962 is an abridged excerpt; Jacob's is full. Prior complete English predates us, so not first.

Our text is Lucan's complete 10-book Pharsalia / De Bello Civili in Latin (1515; books III-X + Vita confirmed in chapters). Canonical complete English translations long predate us: Gorges (1614), Thomas May full 10 books (1627), plus many modern (Riley, Duff Loeb, Braund). Same work, different edition.

Thomas Holcroft's English translation/adaptation of Beaumarchais's La Folle Journee, ou Le Mariage de Figaro was staged at Covent Garden in late 1784 and published 1785 as 'The Follies of a Day; or, The Marriage of Figaro' (same French source, same work). Prior English exists.

Our book is Grotius's Latin Mare Liberum (1633 Leiden compilation, w/ Merula's De Maribus appended). The core work has prior complete English translations: Magoffin's The Freedom of the Seas (1916, Carnegie/Oxford) and Hakluyt's The Free Sea (c.1609-16, pub. Liberty Fund 2004). Not first.

Our book is the Dindorf Greek-Latin original of Aristophanes' eleven comedies. Multiple prior complete English translations exist, notably W. J. Hickie's (Bohn's Classical Library) made directly "from the revised text of Dindorf" — same source text — plus 18th-c. and 1912 versions. Far from first.

Our text is Calcidius's Latin Timaeus (to ~53c) in MS. Digby 23. Magee 2016 (Dumbarton Oaks/Harvard, ISBN 978-0-674-59917-8) is the first English translation of exactly this Calcidius Latin text, bilingual facing-page. Plato's Timaeus also has many prior English versions from the Greek (Jowett, Bury, Cornford). Prior English exists either way.

Our book IS the Henry A. Homes 1873 translation (Albany: Munsell) of Ghazali's Kimiya-yi Sa'adat, made from an-Nawali's Turkish abridgment. Documented as the earliest English rendering; Claud Field's English came later (1909/10). No English predates 1873.

Prior English translation exists: 2018 Univ. of Oregon MA thesis "Las Excelencias de Los Hebreos: An Introduction and Translation of Isaac Cardoso's Seventeenth-Century Apology" — a scholarly English translation of this same Spanish 1679 work. Humanities CORE also hosts English pedagogical editions. Kaplan 1971 is Hebrew (doesn't count).

sources_checked: ETCSL (Oxford Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature)
reason: Our text IS ETCSL 3.3.01 — same title verbatim, and our quotes ("let no one waste my father's household") match the ETCSL English translation word-for-word. ETCSL published this English translation online c.1998–2006, ~20 yrs before our record. Prior English exists.

Our book is the 1558 Venice 'Rime et Prose di Della Casa' (ed. Erasmo Gemini) — a multi-work container bundling the Rime (poems), prose Oratione, and the FIRST printing of the Galateo. Composite anthology = ill-defined first-translation claim. Also the Galateo has English translations since 1576 (Peterson). Metadata wrong: lang is Italian not Latin; author is Della Casa not Gemini.

Catullus, Tibullus, and Propertius are among the most-translated Roman poets; complete English translations long predate us (Loeb vols., Butler's Propertius 1912, 19th-c. verse versions, Wikisource combined edition). Our 1515 Latin trio is a different edition of works already fully in English.

Coherent 1807 French original (Saint-Martin's posthumous collection: self-portrait, Sentences chinoises, Cimetiere d'Amboise, late aphorisms). Translated EN Saint-Martin corpus is finite (Penny/Waite/Stanley) and excludes Oeuvres posthumes and all its constituent texts. No prior English found.

Callimachus' Hymns and Epigrams (our text = Estienne Greek edition) has many prior complete English translations: William Dodd (1755, Hymns + select Epigrams), H.W. Tytler (1793, complete Hymns & Epigrams in verse), Loeb (Mair 1921), Lombardo/Rayor. Prior English long predates us.

Iamblichus' De Mysteriis has multiple prior complete English translations: Thomas Taylor 1821 (2nd ed. 1895), Alexander Wilder 1911, and Clarke/Dillon/Hershbell 2003. Our book is the Greek Parthey critical edition of the same work; not the first English.

Single-year German astrological practica for 1496 (incunabulum, Nuremberg/Creussner; sole holding BSB Munich per ISTC ic00474100). No English edition in ISTC; targeted title/author searches return zero English translation. Ephemeral annual prognostications are essentially never translated. Our 20/21 pages translated = complete.

Virdung's 1495 Practica Cracoviensis is an ephemeral year-specific astrological incunabulum, precisely identified and distinct from his other yearly practicae. No English translation (full or partial, historic or modern) is attested in incunabula catalogs (GW), antiquarian listings, or genre scholarship. Our edition is complete (21/21 pages).

Dorothy Wyckoff's complete English translation of De mineralibus, "Book of Minerals" (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1967), translated directly from the Latin, is well-documented across IA, Smithsonian, and journal reviews. Same work, prior complete English exists.

Ficino's Commentarium in Convivium Platonis de Amore (De Amore, 1475) was translated into English in full by Sears R. Jayne: University of Missouri Studies 1944, reissued Spring Publications 1985. Complete prior English translation of this exact Latin work exists.

Our book is the Greek original of Procopius's Wars Bks III-VIII (Vandal+Gothic Wars), 1905 Haury Teubner. Complete prior English translations from the same Greek exist: H. Holcroft 1653 (Justinian's Warres) and H.B. Dewing, Loeb, 1914-28. Single coherent work, claim well-defined.

Complete prior English translation exists: John Partridge, "Thesaurus & armamentarium medico-chymicum, or, A treasury of physick" (London, 1682), rendered from Mynsicht's Latin original. Same work, same source language, full-text in EEBO-TCP. We are not the first.

Our Vol. 2 is the gynecology section (seeking progeny, fetal nourishment, pregnancy/postpartum) of Sun Simiao's Qianjin Yaofang. Sabine Wilms published a full English translation of Vols. 2-4 (the women's-medicine volumes), ISBN 9780979955204, in 2007/2008 — same work, same content. Prior English exists.
